title: Release Eng: add runtime-1.20-lts branch tooling + protect release/* branches
author: Connor O'Brien
body: Context: Enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private) are asking for a slower-change runtime line; to pilot that we need a repeatable way to cut an LTS branch and ensure release branches can’t be mutated outside the backport workflow. This PR wires up the initial runtime LTS branch tooling and branch protection for `release/*` (including `runtime-1.20-lts`) and documents the cut process for Release Eng + Runtime. What’s in this PR: (1) Add `tools/release/cut_lts_branch.py` to create `runtime-<minor>-lts` from a release cut point, tag an initial `runtime-<minor>-lts.0` RC, and open a tracking issue for the patch train; the script enforces: clean working tree, explicit source ref, and a generated branch summary (base SHA, date, operator, and links). (2) Add GitHub branch protection configuration for `release/*` and `runtime-*-lts` branches: require PRs, require linear history, disallow force-push, require signed commits, require required status checks (see below), and require CODEOWNERS review for runtime-kernel/scheduling + release-eng owned paths. (3) Add release-branch CI workflow (`.github/workflows/release-branch.yml`) that runs on PRs targeting `release/*`: build+unit tests, determinism check, runtime microbench smoke (non-GPU), and a “provenance metadata” job that produces an artifact with build inputs and commit SHAs for audit traceability. (4) Docs: add `docs/release/lts_branching.md` describing naming, the “cut criteria” checklist, and what changes are allowed on LTS branches (bug/security fixes + narrowly scoped perf/stability fixes only). (5) Repo hygiene: CODEOWNERS updates for `tools/release/**` and `docs/release/**`, plus a PR template snippet for LTS cut PRs. Required checks for `release/*`: `lint`, `unit`, `build-linux-x86_64`, `release-branch/determinism`, `release-branch/provenance-metadata` (GPU perf canary will be added in follow-up once perf-canary baselines are landed; see ENG-4827). Notes/constraints: This does not change runtime code paths; it only adds tooling/guardrails. The branch protection rules are scoped to `release/*` so we don’t inadvertently block normal mainline velocity. For the initial pilot we’ll cut `runtime-1.20-lts` off `release/runtime-1.20` once that release is tagged; this PR lays the groundwork and adds a dry-run mode in the script so we can validate permissions in staging. Testing: ran `cut_lts_branch.py --dry-run` locally; CI added/updated workflows; verified branch protection settings via `gh api` on a test repo; docs reviewed by Runtime + SRE. Rollout: after merge, Release Eng will apply the protection rules in the `redwood` repo via admin; then run a dry-run LTS cut and capture logs for audit evidence procedure draft.
commits: release: add cut_lts_branch helper (dry-run + tracking output)
ci: introduce release-branch workflow and required checks for release/*
repo: CODEOWNERS + PR template tweaks for LTS/release branches
docs: add LTS branching + cut checklist doc
security: require signed commits and block force-push on release/*
review_conversation: Sahana Iyer: The determinism job is great, but can we make it fail if `go env` differs between runner images? We’ve been bitten by that when rebuilding release branches.

Connor O'Brien: Good call. Added a step that records `go version`, `rustc --version`, `clang --version`, and fails if the runner image label doesn’t match the pinned set in `tools/release/toolchain_manifest.json`.
Noah Patel: For `runtime-*-lts` protection: do we want to allow maintainers to push emergency commits during an incident? (Sometimes we do this on private forks.)

Connor O'Brien: For the canonical `redwood` repo, I’d like to keep “no direct pushes” as the default so we preserve traceability. For emergency cases we can use an admin override + post-incident backfill, but that should be rare and explicit. Added a note to docs under “Emergency patch procedure (exceptions)”.
Omar El-Sayed: Can the cut script ensure the LTS branch is cut from a release tag, not an arbitrary SHA? That reduces ambiguity for backports later.
Connor O'Brien: Updated: by default the script requires `--from-tag runtime-<minor>.0` unless `--allow-sha` is provided, which is gated behind an env var and prints a loud warning in the summary.
Sean Gallagher: SRE ask: add a placeholder required check for perf gating so the branch protection doesn’t need to be re-tuned later.
Sahana Iyer: -1 to a required check that always runs as “skipped”; it will block merges if anything changes in GitHub semantics. Suggest add it when perf-canary is ready.

Connor O'Brien: Agreed; leaving perf-canary out of required checks for now. Added a clearly named optional job `release-branch/perf-placeholder` that is non-blocking and will be removed once perf-canary is wired (ENG-4827).
Marcus Lin: Security: please ensure the provenance job captures artifact hashes and the exact container image digest used for the build job.

Connor O'Brien: Done. The provenance artifact now includes build container image digest (`.github/workflows` runner image), `git describe`, and SHA256 for the produced runtime tarball (when built in CI).
timeline: 2026-01-19: CI added for release/* branches; initial determinism job failing due to unpinned toolchain metadata
2026-01-20: Fix determinism job + add toolchain manifest
2026-01-21: Security review updates provenance artifact and branch protection settings
2026-01-22: Final approvals; squashed and merged to main
